segments.text:
Alſo if our aduerſaries opinion ſhould be admitted, it might not be auoided, but that aſwell the wicked as the godly ſhoulde eate and drinke the fleſh and bloud of the Lord. But this doeth Chriſt the Author of the ſacraments manifeſtly refute in the 6. of
Iohn, where he ſaieth that his fleſh and bloud is eaten and drunken by faith. See then (I pray you) that when ye wicked are deſtitute of faith, and be ſtraungers from Chriſt, what communion haue they with the fleſh and bloud of Chriſt? Doubtleſſe they haue onely the ſignes to be receiued, and that to their owne condemnation: for neither is Chriſt in them, neyther doe they abide in Chriſt.
